title: The Thomas Christians
hook: the Syro-Malabar and Syro-Malankara churches of India trace their faith to Thomas

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Maronites: a church of Lebanon, named for a hermit, that says it never left communion with Rome. Your line was the cedars. Where did you stand your ground? Day one thousand three hundred sixty-four.

Kerala, on the southwest coast of India. Coconut palms, backwaters, rain that arrives like a wall. A bride in a gold-bordered sari walks out of a church, and her family has kept the faith for as long as anyone can say. Ask them where it came from, and they won't say Portugal, or England, or a missionary from Europe. They'll name an apostle. Thomas, they'll tell you. He came here. Some of their churches even carry his name over the door. For anyone who thinks of the faith as having traveled out of Rome, it's a surprise to meet Christians whose story starts somewhere else entirely. Today, the people who call themselves his children.
screen: `A WEDDING IN KERALA.` → `NOT EUROPE. AN APOSTLE.` → `THOMAS, THEY SAY.`

segments.voice: Thomas, as the Gospels show him, is more than a doubter. When Jesus decides to go back toward danger in Judea, John's Gospel gives Thomas the brave line: "Let us also go, that we may die with him." Later, yes, he says he won't believe the resurrection until he touches the wounds. But when he sees Jesus, he says, in the Douay-Rheims, "My Lord, and my God." Bold, then doubting, then a confession that calls Jesus Lord and God. Next, India. The Gospels end before Thomas's travels begin. Ancient tradition says he sailed east and preached on the Malabar coast, and the Christians of Kerala keep that memory, with places and songs tied to his name. Scholars debate the history; the families don't need them to settle it to know who they are. Then the churches. Today, two Eastern Catholic churches belong to this family. The Syro-Malabar Church prays in the East Syriac tradition. The Syro-Malankara Church prays in the West Syriac tradition. Both call their Eucharist the Holy Qurbana. And not every Thomas Christian is Catholic: Orthodox and other churches share the same heritage, and the same apostle. Last, what they've kept. These are Christians who are fully Indian, at home in a land of many faiths, with customs drawn from their own soil, and fully Catholic too. The faith wasn't imported, they'd say. It grew here, from a seed an apostle planted.
screen: `LET US ALSO GO, THAT WE MAY DIE WITH HIM.` · `TRADITION: THOMAS SAILED TO INDIA.` · `SYRO-MALABAR AND SYRO-MALANKARA.` · `FULLY INDIAN, FULLY CATHOLIC.` · then, large: `MY LORD, AND MY GOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for India, or simply turn toward it. Settle, and breathe. Picture the subcontinent from above: mountains in the north, the long coasts, cities full to bursting, villages at dusk. Its Christians live among neighbors of many faiths. Let the whole of it in, without picking favorites. If you pray, you can pray for India and all its people, and you might borrow Thomas's words, my Lord, and my God, as he said them. If you don't, simply wish the whole country well, whatever hour it is there now. The bell holds the time.

The Thomas Christians. The ancient Christians of Kerala, in India, who trace their faith to the apostle Thomas. Two of their churches are Eastern Catholic: the Syro-Malabar and the Syro-Malankara. Today's word.
Your line: thomas's children. Today, when you doubt, remember the man who doubted out loud and still ended up saying, my Lord, and my God. Day one thousand three hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: Syro-Malabar Catholics celebrate the Holy Qurbana in the East Syriac tradition and Syro-Malankara Catholics in the West Syriac tradition, mostly in Malayalam; both churches honor Saint Thomas as the apostle who, by their tradition, brought the faith to India.

notes: Thomas's mission to India is presented as ancient tradition held by Kerala's Christians 'for centuries' (no date or number); 'scholars debate the history'. Confirm framing.
Syro-Malabar = East Syriac tradition; Syro-Malankara = West Syriac tradition; both call the Eucharist Holy Qurbana. Confirm.
'Not every Thomas Christian is Catholic: Orthodox and other churches share the same heritage' (e.g. Malankara Orthodox, Jacobite Syrian, Mar Thoma). Confirm the wording is fair to them.
Hook mentions churches named for Thomas and a bride in a gold-bordered sari; general picture of Kerala Christian life. Confirm it reads respectfully.
howItsDone says the liturgy is 'mostly in Malayalam': confirm.
Douay-Rheims wording of John 11:16 and 20:28: confirm.
Original: Δίδυμος, 'twin', from John 11:16 ('Thomas, who is called Didymus'). Confirm the pronunciation.
